svg.title: ScheduleIO entity relationship diagram
svg.desc: A scalable entity relationship diagram and complete attribute catalog for the ScheduleIO project model, including primary keys, foreign keys, project and task fields, owned value records, calendars, assignments, dependencies, and view state.
svg.text: Complete model map · scalar attributes · stable identities · explicit and collection-owned links
ScheduleIO stores a value model; owned values are not separate SQL tables.

g.text: tasks · resources · assignments · relations · calendars · customFieldDefinitions
value collections scoped to their owning record

svg.text: Core entities and every public attribute
PK = stable uniqueId; FK = UID reference. Project is the root document and has no standalone UID.

g.text: Root document · no standalone primary key · options, collections, opaque preservation, and view state
PK uniqueId · id is display order; outlineLevel and WBS describe hierarchy without a parent FK
PK uniqueId · associative record connecting one task to one resource
PK uniqueId · cost, availability, baselines, and resource calendar
PK uniqueId · working week, exceptions, and optional base calendar
How to read the complete attribute catalog
• Yellow PK marks a stable UID; PK* marks a scoped or composite key in a value collection.
• Teal FK marks an explicit UID reference to another core entity.
• Lists are owned values. Their owner is implied by the containing Project, Task, Resource, Assignment, or Calendar collection.
• Collection records without a declared UID use owner scope and, where shown, a conceptual natural/composite key (PK*).
• Task.id is a display/outline position, not a primary key. Task hierarchy has no parentTaskUid field.

svg.text: Owned value records and their complete attributes
Each record below is stored in an owner collection; no standalone PK is declared unless a member is marked.
These nested value objects are Project or Task attributes, shown here with every public member.
Primary and foreign key labels describe ScheduleIO model identity and references. Owned-value keys shown in the notes are conceptual ER projections, not declared SQL constraints.
